question: Which of the following methods of particle size reduction in a powder mixture get smaller size ranges ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Cutting methods -> typically produce larger particles -> less effective for fine size reduction -> 60%
CHAIN: Compression methods -> apply pressure to particles -> can create smaller particles through deformation -> moderate effectiveness for size reduction -> 70%
CHAIN: Impact methods -> involve high-speed collisions -> break particles into smaller sizes -> generally effective for fine size reduction -> 85%
CHAIN: Methods of friction -> generate heat and shear forces -> can lead to smaller particle sizes through abrasion -> effective but may vary based on material -> 75%
analysis: Impact methods are generally more effective for achieving smaller particle size ranges in powder mixtures due to the high energy involved in the process, which can break down particles more efficiently compared to cutting, compression, or friction methods.
